title: How to organise the fastener and hardware zone | Workshop
description:
Let you put your hand on the right screw straight away, so a project never stops for a hardware run.

This is the Fastener and Hardware Zone in the Workshop. About 45-75 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
One fastener type and size per compartment, with a sample screw glued to the outside of each drawer face so you match by eye rather than by reading. Deck screws separate from drywall screws, no coffee tin of mixed hardware anywhere on the shelf, and a marked minimum line inside the compartments you empty most.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Empty the mixed jars onto a tray and keep only what you can name confidently by size and type.
Straighten: Sort by type first and size second, with the sizes you drive weekly at hand height and the specialty hinges an
Shine: Vacuum the drawers of metal filings and grit, and look for rust bloom in the bottom corners; if you find it, t
Safety: A wall cabinet full of steel fasteners is far heavier than it looks, so fix it into studs rather than plasterb
Standardize: One compartment per size, no exceptions and no shared drawers, with a minimum line marked inside so a low bin
Sustain: The handful of leftover fasteners in your pocket goes back into its compartment before the tools go back on th

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
One size per compartment, a sample fastener on the front, and a minimum line inside.

Full written steps for this zone, free:
https://6s-success.com/zones/workshop-the-fastener-and-hardware-zone.html

6S Success turns Lean's six-S method into something you can actually do in a house: Sort, Straighten, Shine, Safety, Standardize, Sustain. One small zone at a time, finished in one session, and it stays finished.
